sanskrit: nityam eva sukhaṃ svarge sukhaṃ duḥkham ihobhayam narake duḥkham evāhuḥ samaṃ tu paramaṃ padam
english: In heaven there is unbroken happiness; here below both happiness and sorrow; in hell, they say, there is sorrow alone—but the supreme state is poised beyond them all, in perfect equanimity.

sanskrit: pṛthivī sarvabhūtānāṃ janitrī tadvidhāḥ striyaḥ pumān prajāpatis tatra śukraṃ tejomayaṃ viduḥ
english: The earth is the mother of all beings, and women are of her nature; the male is Prajāpati, the lord of creatures, and in him they know the seed to be a thing made of radiant fire.

sanskrit: ity etal lokanirmāṇaṃ brahmaṇā vihitaṃ purā prajā viparivartante svaiḥ svaiḥ karmabhir āvṛtāḥ
english: Such is the fashioning of the worlds, ordained of old by Brahmā; and creatures revolve through their births, each one enveloped by its own deeds.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca dānasya kiṃ phalaṃ prāhur dharmasya caritasya ca tapasaś ca sutaptasya svādhyāyasya hutasya ca
english: Bharadvāja said: What fruit do they declare for giving, for the practice of dharma duly performed, for austerity well undergone, for recitation of the Veda, and for oblation offered into fire?

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ svādhyāye śāntir uttamā dānena bhoga ity āhus tapasā sarvam āpnuyāt
english: Bhṛgu said: By oblation sin is allayed; in recitation of the Veda is the highest peace; by giving, they say, comes enjoyment; and by austerity a man may attain all things.

sanskrit: dānaṃ tu dvividhaṃ prāhuḥ paratrārtham ihaiva ca sadbhyo yad dīyate kiṃ cit tat paratropatiṣṭhati
english: Giving, they declare, is of two kinds: for the next world and for this. Whatever is given to the good awaits its giver in the world beyond.

sanskrit: asatsu dīyate yat tu tad dānam iha bhujyate yādṛśaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tādṛśaṃ phalam āpyate
english: But the gift that is given to the unworthy yields its enjoyment here below; for as a gift is given, so is the fruit obtained.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca kiṃ kasya dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃ vā dharmasya lakṣaṇam dharmaḥ katividho vāpi tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Bharadvāja said: What is the practice of dharma, and for whom? What is the mark of dharma? And of how many kinds is dharma? This you ought to tell me.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca svadharmacaraṇe yuktā ye bhavanti manīṣiṇaḥ teṣāṃ dharmaphalāvāptir yo 'nyathā sa vimuhyati
english: Bhṛgu said: Those wise ones who are devoted to the practice of their own dharma obtain the fruit of dharma; but he who does otherwise falls into bewilderment.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca yad etac cāturāśramyaṃ brahmarṣivihitaṃ purā teṣāṃ sve sve ya ācārās tān me vaktum ihārhasi
english: Bharadvāja said: As for this system of the four stages of life, ordained of old by the brahmin sages—the observances proper to each of them you ought now to tell me.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca pūrvam eva bhagavatā lokahitam anutiṣṭhatā dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārtham āśramāś catvāro 'bhinirdiṣṭāḥ tatra gurukulavāsam eva tāvat prathamam āśramam udāharanti samyag atra śaucasaṃskāravinayaniyamapraṇīto vinītātmā ubhe saṃdhye bhāskarāgnidaivatāny upasthāya vihāya tandrālasye guror abhivādanavedābhyāsaśravaṇapavitrīkṛtāntarātmā triṣavaṇam upaspṛśya brahmacaryāgniparicaraṇaguruśuśrūṣānityo bhaikṣādisarvaniveditāntarātmā guruvacananirdeśānuṣṭhānāpratikūlo guruprasādalabdhasvādhyāyatatparaḥ syāt
english: Bhṛgu said: Of old, by the Blessed One who acts for the welfare of the worlds, the four stages of life were appointed for the protection of dharma. Among these they name first the stage of dwelling in the teacher's house: there, rightly disciplined in purity, rite, modesty, and restraint, his self subdued, the student should at both twilights wait upon the sun, the fire, and the gods; casting off sloth and torpor, with his inmost being purified by salutation to the teacher, by study and the hearing of the Veda, he should touch water at the three sacred junctures of the day, ever devoted to the vow of chastity, to the tending of the sacred fire, and to service of his teacher; offering up to his teacher all that he gathers by begging and the rest, never adverse to carrying out the teacher's word and command, and intent upon that recitation which he wins by his teacher's grace.

sanskrit: guruṃ yas tu samārādhya dvijo vedam avāpnuyāt bhavati cātra ślokaḥ tasya svargaphalāvāptiḥ sidhyate cāsya mānasam
english: The twice-born who, propitiating his teacher, attains the Veda—of him there is this verse: he wins the fruit of heaven, and his heart's desire is fulfilled.

sanskrit: gārhasthyaṃ khalu dvitīyam āśramaṃ vadanti tasya samudācāralakṣaṇaṃ sarvam anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ samāvṛttānāṃ sadārāṇāṃ sahadharmacaryāphalārthināṃ gṛhāśramo vidhīyate dharmārthakāmāvāptir hy atra trivargasādhanam avekṣyāgarhitena karmaṇā dhanāny ādāya svādhyāyaprakarṣopalabdhena brahmarṣinirmitena vā adrisāragatena vā havyaniyamābhyāsadaivataprasādopalabdhena vā dhanena gṛhastho gārhasthyaṃ pravartayet tad dhi sarvāśramāṇāṃ mūlam udāharanti gurukulavāsinaḥ parivrājakā ye cānye saṃkalpitavrataniyamadharmānuṣṭhāyinas teṣām apy ata eva bhikṣābalisaṃvibhāgāḥ pravartante
english: The householder's life, indeed, they call the second stage; all the marks of its proper conduct we shall expound. For those who have completed their studentship and taken wives, who seek the fruit of practising dharma together, the household stage is ordained. Here is the attainment of dharma, wealth, and desire—the means to the threefold aim. With regard to that, taking wealth by blameless action—wealth won through eminence in Vedic recitation, or made by brahmin sages, or drawn from the heart of the mountains, or gained by the grace of the gods through the practice of oblation and restraint—the householder should carry on his household life. For this, they declare, is the root of all the stages of life; for from it alone do the shares of alms and offering proceed even to those who dwell in the teacher's house, to wandering mendicants, and to all others who keep their vows, restraints, and resolved observances of dharma.

sanskrit: vānaprasthānāṃ dravyopaskāra iti prāyaśaḥ khalv ete sādhavaḥ sādhupathyadarśanāḥ svādhyāyaprasaṅginas tīrthābhigamanadeśadarśanārthaṃ pṛthivīṃ paryaṭanti teṣāṃ pratyutthānābhivādanānasūyāvākpradānasaumukhyaśaktyāsanaśayanābhyavahārasatkriyāś ceti
english: And there is the furnishing of goods to the forest-dwellers. For the most part these are holy men, beholders of the good and wholesome path, devoted to recitation of the Veda, who roam the earth to visit the sacred fords and to behold its regions; toward them are owed the rising up to greet them, salutation, freedom from envy, gracious speech, a kindly face, and the honour, according to one's means, of a seat, a bed, and food.

sanskrit: atithir yasya bhagnāśo gṛhāt pratinivartate bhavati cātra ślokaḥ sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyam ādāya gacchati
english: From whose house a guest turns away, his hope broken—of this there is a verse: that guest, leaving his own ill deed behind for the host, departs taking the host's merit with him.

sanskrit: api cātra yajñakriyābhir devatāḥ prīyante nivāpena pitaro vedābhyāsaśravaṇadhāraṇena ṛṣayaḥ apatyotpādanena prajāpatir iti
english: Moreover, in this stage the gods are gladdened by the rites of sacrifice, the ancestors by funerary offerings, the seers by the study, hearing, and retention of the Veda, and Prajāpati by the begetting of offspring.

sanskrit: vatsalāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vācyāḥ śrotrasukhā giraḥ ślokau cātra bhavataḥ parivādopaghātau ca pāruṣyaṃ cātra garhitam
english: Tender toward all beings, one should speak words pleasant to the ear; and here there are two verses on this: slander and injury, and harshness too, are here condemned.

sanskrit: avajñānam ahaṃkāro dambhaś caiva vigarhitaḥ ahiṃsā satyam akrodhaḥ sarvāśramagataṃ tapaḥ
english: Contempt, egotism, and hypocrisy are blamed; but non-violence, truth, and freedom from anger are the austerity that belongs to every stage of life.

sanskrit: api cātra mālyābharaṇavastrābhyaṅgagandhopabhoganṛttagītavāditraśrutisukhanayanābhirāmasaṃdarśanānāṃ prāptir bhakṣyabhojyapeyalehyacoṣyāṇām abhyavahāryāṇāṃ vividhānām upabhogaḥ svadāravihārasaṃtoṣaḥ kāmasukhāvāptir iti
english: And in this stage too there is the having of garlands, ornaments, garments, unguents, and perfumes; the delights of dancing, song, and music; sights that ravish the ear and please the eye; the enjoyment of foods of every kind—to be chewed, eaten, drunk, licked, and sucked; the contentment of dalliance with one's own wife; and the attainment of the pleasures of desire.

sanskrit: trivargaguṇanirvṛttir yasya nityaṃ gṛhāśrame sa sukhāny anubhūyeha śiṣṭānāṃ gatim āpnuyāt
english: He in whose household life the qualities of the threefold aim are ever fulfilled—he, having known its joys here, attains the destiny of the virtuous.

sanskrit: uñchavṛttir gṛhastho yaḥ svadharmacaraṇe rataḥ tyaktakāmasukhārambhas tasya svargo na durlabhaḥ
english: The householder who lives by gleaning, delighting in the practice of his own dharma, who has renounced the pursuit of sensual pleasure—for him heaven is not hard to win.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca vānaprasthāḥ khalu ṛṣidharmam anusarantaḥ puṇyāni tīrthāni nadīprasravaṇāni suvivikteṣv araṇyeṣu mṛgamahiṣavarāhasṛmaragajākīrṇeṣu tapasyanto 'nusaṃcaranti tyaktagrāmyavastrāhāropabhogā vanyauṣadhimūlaphalaparṇaparimitavicitraniyatāhārāḥ sthānāsanino bhūmipāṣāṇasikatāśarkarāvālukābhasmaśāyinaḥ kāśakuśacarmavalkalasaṃvṛtāṅgāḥ keśaśmaśrunakharomadhāriṇo niyatakālopasparśanā askannahomabalikālānuṣṭhāyinaḥ samitkuśakusumopahārahomārjanalabdhaviśrāmāḥ śītoṣṇapavananiṣṭaptavibhinnasarvatvaco vividhaniyamayogacaryāvihitadharmānuṣṭhānahṛtamāṃsaśoṇitās tvagasthibhūtā dhṛtiparāḥ sattvayogāc charīrāṇy udvahanti
english: Bhṛgu said: The forest-dwellers, following the dharma of the seers, roam practising austerity by the holy fords, the rivers and their springs, in well-secluded forests thronged with deer, buffalo, boar, wild antelope, and elephant. Having renounced the garments, food, and enjoyments of the village, they keep a measured, varied, and regulated diet of wild herbs, roots, fruit, and leaves. They stand or sit at their stations, sleeping on bare earth, on stones, gravel, sand, grit, or ashes, their bodies clad in kāśa and kuśa grass, in skins and bark, wearing their hair, beard, nails, and body-hair uncut. They touch water at the appointed times and perform without lapse the rites of oblation and offering at their due hours; their rest is won amid the gathering of fuel, kuśa grass, and flowers, the offering of oblations, and the cleansing for it. Their skin everywhere scorched and cracked by cold, heat, and wind, their flesh and blood worn away by the performance of dharma ordained in manifold restraints, disciplines of yoga, and observances, reduced to skin and bone yet supreme in steadfastness, they bear up their bodies by the power of their inner being.

sanskrit: yas tv etāṃ niyataś caryāṃ brahmarṣivihitāṃ caret sa dahed agnivad doṣāñ jayel lokāṃś ca durjayān
english: And he who, self-restrained, follows this course of conduct ordained by the brahmin sages would burn away his faults as fire consumes, and would conquer the worlds that are hard to conquer.

sanskrit: parivrājakānāṃ punar ācāras tad yathā vimucyāgnidhanakalatraparibarhasaṅgān ātmanaḥ snehapāśān avadhūya parivrajanti samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanās trivargapravṛtteṣv ārambheṣv asaktabuddhayo 'rimitrodāsīneṣu tulyavṛttayaḥ sthāvarajarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjānāṃ bhūtānāṃ vāṅmanaḥkarmabhir anabhidrohiṇo 'niketāḥ parvatapulinavṛkṣamūladevatāyatanāny anucaranto vāsārtham upeyur nagaraṃ grāmaṃ vā nagare pañcarātrikā grāmaikarātrikāḥ praviśya ca prāṇadhāraṇamātrārthaṃ dvijātīnāṃ bhavanāny asaṃkīrṇakarmaṇām upatiṣṭheyuḥ pātrapatitāyācitabhaikṣāḥ kāmakrodhadarpamohalobhakārpaṇyadambhaparivādābhimānahiṃsānivṛttā iti
english: Again, such is the conduct of the wandering mendicants: loosing themselves from attachment to fire, wealth, wife, and retinue, and shaking off the bonds of their own affection, they go forth as wanderers. To them a clod, a stone, and gold are all alike; their minds unattached to undertakings aimed at the threefold worldly aim, they bear themselves equally toward foe, friend, and the indifferent. By word, thought, and deed they do no harm to any beings—those born from the womb, from eggs, from sweat, those that sprout from the ground, or those that stand unmoving. Homeless, frequenting the mountains, the river-sands, the roots of trees, and the shrines of the gods, they go for lodging to a town or a village—five nights in a town, a single night in a village—and entering it, only to sustain their breath of life, they wait at the dwellings of the twice-born whose works are unmixed, taking such alms as fall unasked into their bowl, having turned away from desire, anger, pride, delusion, greed, meanness, hypocrisy, slander, conceit, and violence.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā carati yo muniḥ bhavati cātra ślokaḥ na tasya sarvabhūtebhyo bhayam utpadyate kva cit
english: The sage who goes his way having granted freedom from fear to all beings—of him there is this verse: from no beings whatsoever does fear ever arise for him.

sanskrit: kṛtvāgnihotraṃ svaśarīrasaṃsthaṃ; śārīram agniṃ svamukhe juhoti yo bhaikṣacaryopagatair havirbhiś; citāgnināṃ sa vyatiyāti lokān
english: Having made the fire-offering reside within his own body, he who pours oblations into the fire of the body through his own mouth, with the offerings gathered in his round of begging, surpasses the worlds of those who tend the fire of the altar.

sanskrit: mokṣāśramaṃ yaḥ kurute yathoktaṃ; śuciḥ susaṃkalpitabuddhiyuktaḥ anindhanaṃ jyotir iva praśāntaṃ; sa brahmalokaṃ śrayate dvijātiḥ
english: The twice-born who keeps the stage of liberation as it has been declared—pure, endowed with a well-resolved understanding—comes to rest in the world of Brahman, serene like a flame with no fuel to feed it.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca asmāl lokāt paro lokaḥ śrūyate nopalabhyate tam ahaṃ jñātum icchāmi tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Bharadvāja said: A world beyond this world is heard of, yet is not seen. That world I wish to know; this you ought to tell me.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca uttare himavatpārśve puṇye sarvaguṇānvite puṇyaḥ kṣemyaś ca kāmyaś ca sa varo loka ucyate
english: Bhṛgu said: On the northern slope of the Himavat, a holy region endowed with every excellence, there lies a land that is holy, secure, and lovely—it is called the most blessed of worlds.

sanskrit: tatra hy apāpakarmāṇaḥ śucayo 'tyantanirmalāḥ lobhamohaparityaktā mānavā nirupadravāḥ
english: For there the people are free of sinful deeds, pure, utterly spotless, abandoned by greed and delusion, and untouched by any affliction.

sanskrit: sa svargasadṛśo deśas tatra hy uktāḥ śubhā guṇāḥ kāle mṛtyuḥ prabhavati spṛśanti vyādhayo na ca
english: That land is like heaven, for there, it is said, are auspicious qualities: death prevails only in its due time, and diseases do not touch them.

sanskrit: na lobhaḥ paradāreṣu svadāranirato janaḥ na cānyonyavadhas tatra dravyeṣu na ca vismayaḥ parokṣadharmo naivāsti saṃdeho nāpi jāyate
english: There is no coveting of others' wives; each man delights in his own wife. There is no slaying of one another, and no greed for goods; no dharma performed merely for show exists there, nor does doubt ever arise.

sanskrit: kṛtasya tu phalaṃ tatra pratyakṣam upalabhyate śayyāyānāsanopetāḥ prāsādabhavanāśrayāḥ sarvakāmair vṛtāḥ ke cid dhemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: There the fruit of what is done is obtained before one's very eyes: some, furnished with couches, vehicles, and seats, dwelling in palaces and mansions, are surrounded by all that they desire, adorned with ornaments of gold.

sanskrit: prāṇadhāraṇamātraṃ tu keṣāṃ cid upapadyate śrameṇa mahatā ke cit kurvanti prāṇadhāraṇam
english: To some there falls but enough to sustain the breath of life; and some, with great toil, manage barely to keep themselves alive.

sanskrit: iha dharmaparāḥ ke cit ke cin naikṛtikā narāḥ sukhitā duḥkhitāḥ ke cin nirdhanā dhanino 'pare
english: Here below some men are devoted to dharma, others are deceitful; some are happy, some are wretched; some are without wealth, while others are rich.

sanskrit: iha śramo bhayaṃ mohaḥ kṣudhā tīvrā ca jāyate lobhaś cārthakṛto nṝṇāṃ yena muhyanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: Here arise toil, fear, delusion, and sharp hunger, and the greed of men bred of wealth, by which even the wise are led astray.

sanskrit: iha cintā bahuvidhā dharmādharmasya karmaṇaḥ yas tad vedobhayaṃ prājñaḥ pāpmanā na sa lipyate
english: Here is anxiety of many kinds over deeds of dharma and of unrighteousness; the wise man who understands them both is not stained by sin.

sanskrit: sopadhaṃ nikṛtiḥ steyaṃ parivādo 'bhyasūyatā paropaghāto hiṃsā ca paiśunyam anṛtaṃ tathā
english: Fraud with concealed design, deceit, theft, slander, fault-finding, the injuring of others, violence, calumny, and falsehood—

sanskrit: etān āsevate yas tu tapas tasya prahīyate yas tv etān nācared vidvāṃs tapas tasyābhivardhate
english: he who indulges in these, his austerity wastes away; but the learned man who does not commit them, his austerity grows ever greater.

sanskrit: karmabhūmir iyaṃ loka iha kṛtvā śubhāśubham śubhaiḥ śubham avāpnoti kṛtvāśubham ato 'nyathā
english: This world is the field of action; having done here what is good or evil, by good deeds one attains good, and by doing evil, the opposite.

sanskrit: iha prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tathā iṣṭveṣṭatapasaḥ pūtā brahmalokam upāśritāḥ
english: Here of old Prajāpati, and the gods together with the hosts of seers, having sacrificed and offered up their austerity, were purified and took their refuge in the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: uttaraḥ pṛthivībhāgaḥ sarvapuṇyatamaḥ śubhaḥ ihatyās tatra jāyante ye vai puṇyakṛto janāḥ
english: The northern region of the earth is the holiest and most blessed of all; there are born those people of this world who are doers of meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: asatkarmāṇi kurvantas tiryagyoniṣu cāpare kṣīṇāyuṣas tathaivānye naśyanti pṛthivītale
english: But others, doing evil deeds, are born in the wombs of beasts; and yet others, their span of life run out, perish upon the face of the earth.

sanskrit: anyonyabhakṣaṇe saktā lobhamohasamanvitāḥ ihaiva parivartante na te yānty uttarāṃ diśam
english: Bent on devouring one another, possessed by greed and delusion, they revolve here below alone; they do not go to that northern quarter.

sanskrit: ye gurūn upasevante niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ panthānaṃ sarvalokānāṃ te jānanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Those wise ones who, self-restrained and chaste, wait upon their teachers—they come to know the path to all the worlds.

sanskrit: ity ukto 'yaṃ mayā dharmaḥ saṃkṣepād brahmanirmitaḥ dharmādharmau hi lokasya yo vai vetti sa buddhimān
english: Thus has this dharma, fashioned by Brahmā, been told by me in brief; for he who truly knows the dharma and the unrighteousness of the world, he is the wise one.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto bhṛguṇā rājan bharadvājaḥ pratāpavān bhṛguṃ paramadharmātmā vismitaḥ pratyapūjayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Bhṛgu, O king, the valiant Bharadvāja, that soul of highest dharma, in wonder paid homage to Bhṛgu in return.

sanskrit: eṣa te prabhavo rājañ jagataḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ nikhilena mahāprājña kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: This, O king, is the origin of the world, declared to you in full, O greatly wise one. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ācārasya vidhiṃ tāta procyamānaṃ tvayānagha śrotum icchāmi dharmajña sarvajño hy asi me mataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The rule of right conduct, dear father, as you would set it forth, I wish to hear, O sinless one who knows the dharma; for in my judgment you are the knower of all things.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca durācārā durviceṣṭā duṣprajñāḥ priyasāhasāḥ asanto hy abhivikhyātāḥ santaś cācāralakṣaṇāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Men of evil conduct, of evil deeds, of corrupt understanding, fond of reckless ventures—these are known abroad as the wicked; the good are marked by their right conduct.

sanskrit: purīṣaṃ yadi vā mūtraṃ ye na kurvanti mānavāḥ rājamārge gavāṃ madhye dhānyamadhye ca te śubhāḥ
english: Those men who pass neither dung nor urine on the king's highway, among cattle, or amid the grain—they are the virtuous.

sanskrit: śaucam āvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā devatānāṃ ca tarpaṇam dharmam āhur manuṣyāṇām upaspṛśya nadīṃ taret
english: Having performed the required cleansing and the satisfying of the gods with libations—this they call the dharma of men—one should touch water and so cross the river.

sanskrit: sūryaṃ sadopatiṣṭheta na svapyād bhāskarodaye sāyaṃ prātar japan saṃdhyāṃ tiṣṭhet pūrvāṃ tathāparām
english: One should ever wait upon the sun, and should not sleep at the rising of the day-maker; murmuring the twilight prayer at evening and at dawn, one should keep both the first and the latter junctures of the day.

sanskrit: pañcārdro bhojanaṃ kuryāt prāṅmukho maunam āsthitaḥ na ninded annabhakṣyāṃś ca svādv asvādu ca bhakṣayet
english: Moistened in the five places, facing east and keeping silence, one should take one's meal; one should not disparage food and victuals, but should eat both the savoury and the unsavoury.

sanskrit: nārdrapāṇiḥ samuttiṣṭhen nārdrapādaḥ svapen niśi devarṣināradaproktam etad ācāralakṣaṇam
english: One should not rise up with wet hands, nor sleep at night with wet feet—this mark of right conduct was declared by the divine seer Nārada.

sanskrit: śucikāmam anaḍvāhaṃ devagoṣṭhaṃ catuṣpatham brāhmaṇaṃ dhārmikaṃ caiva nityaṃ kuryāt pradakṣiṇam
english: A draught-ox that loves cleanliness, a temple-stall of the gods, a crossing of four roads, and a righteous brahmin—about these one should ever make the rightward circuit of reverence.

sanskrit: atithīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ preṣyāṇāṃ svajanasya ca sāmānyaṃ bhojanaṃ bhṛtyaiḥ puruṣasya praśasyate
english: To share food in common with all guests, with servants, with one's own kin, and with dependants—this is praised in a man.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātar manuṣyāṇām aśanaṃ devanirmitam nāntarā bhojanaṃ dṛṣṭam upavāsī tathā bhavet
english: At evening and at dawn is the eating ordained by the gods for men; no meal between these is sanctioned, and so one becomes as a faster.

sanskrit: homakāle tathā juhvann ṛtukāle tathā vrajan ananyastrījanaḥ prājño brahmacārī tathā bhavet
english: Offering oblation at the time of oblation, and approaching his wife at her fertile season, the wise man who has no traffic with any other woman becomes thereby as a celibate.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ brāhmaṇocchiṣṭaṃ jananyā hṛdayaṃ kṛtam upāsīta janaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ santa upāsate
english: The leavings of a brahmin's meal are as nectar, made as it were the very heart of one's mother. Let a man wait upon truth; truth it is that the good revere.

sanskrit: yajuṣā saṃskṛtaṃ māṃsaṃ nivṛtto māṃsabhakṣaṇāt na bhakṣayed vṛthāmāṃsaṃ pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ ca varjayet
english: Flesh consecrated with the sacrificial formula one who has turned away from the eating of flesh may take; but he should not eat flesh slain in vain, and should shun the flesh of the back.

sanskrit: svadeśe paradeśe vā atithiṃ nopavāsayet kāmyaṃ karmaphalaṃ labdhvā gurūṇām upapādayet
english: Whether in one's own land or in another's, one should not let a guest go fasting; having won the fruit of voluntary rites, one should render it up to one's elders.

sanskrit: gurubhya āsanaṃ deyaṃ kartavyaṃ cābhivādanam gurūn abhyarcya yujyante āyuṣā yaśasā śriyā
english: To one's elders a seat should be given, and salutation should be made; those who honour their elders are blessed with long life, with fame, and with fortune.

sanskrit: nekṣetādityam udyantaṃ na ca nagnāṃ parastriyam maithunaṃ samaye dharmyaṃ guhyaṃ caiva samācaret
english: One should not gaze upon the rising sun, nor upon another's wife unclothed; and the lawful union one should practise in its proper season and in secret.

sanskrit: tīrthānāṃ hṛdayaṃ tīrthaṃ śucīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ śuciḥ sarvam āryakṛtaṃ śaucaṃ vālasaṃsparśanāni ca
english: The holy ford of fords is the heart; the pure thing among pure things is the heart. All purification is that wrought by the noble, even down to the touching of a hair.

sanskrit: darśane darśane nityaṃ sukhapraśnam udāharet sāyaṃ prātaś ca viprāṇāṃ pradiṣṭam abhivādanam
english: At every meeting one should ever utter a kindly inquiry after another's welfare; and to the brahmins, at evening and at dawn, salutation is prescribed.

sanskrit: devagoṣṭhe gavāṃ madhye brāhmaṇānāṃ kriyāpathe svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇim uddharet
english: In the temple-stall of the gods, among cattle, in the course of the brahmins' rites, in Vedic recitation, and in eating, one should keep the right hand uplifted.

sanskrit: paṇyānāṃ śobhanaṃ paṇyaṃ kṛṣīṇāṃ bādyate kṛṣiḥ bahukāraṃ ca sasyānāṃ vāhye vāhyaṃ tathā gavām
english: Of wares one should praise the goodly ware; of tillage, that the ploughing prospers; of crops, that they yield abundantly; and of cattle, that the draught-beast draws well.

sanskrit: saṃpannaṃ bhojane nityaṃ pānīye tarpaṇaṃ tathā suśṛtaṃ pāyase brūyād yavāgvāṃ kṛsare tathā
english: At a meal one should always say it is well-furnished; of the drink, that it satisfies; of the milk-rice, gruel, and pottage of sesame and rice, that they are well-cooked.

sanskrit: śmaśrukarmaṇi saṃprāpte kṣute snāne 'tha bhojane vyādhitānāṃ ca sarveṣām āyuṣyam abhinandanam
english: When the trimming of the beard is undertaken, when one sneezes, at bathing, and at eating, and for all the sick, a blessing of long life is the fitting greeting.

sanskrit: pratyādityaṃ na meheta na paśyed ātmanaḥ śakṛt sutastriyā ca śayanaṃ sahabhojyaṃ ca varjayet
english: One should not make water facing the sun, nor look upon one's own ordure; and one should shun lying upon the same couch with a son's wife, and eating together with her.

sanskrit: tvaṃkāraṃ nāmadheyaṃ ca jyeṣṭhānāṃ parivarjayet avarāṇāṃ samānānām ubhayeṣāṃ na duṣyati
english: The familiar "thou" and the calling by name one should avoid toward elders; toward inferiors and equals, with both alike, there is no fault in it.

sanskrit: hṛdayaṃ pāpavṛttānāṃ pāpam ākhyāti vaikṛtam jñānapūrvaṃ vinaśyanti gūhamānā mahājane
english: The heart of those of sinful conduct betrays their sin by its disturbance; knowingly concealing it before the assembled people, they come to ruin.

sanskrit: jñānapūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ chādayanty abahuśrutāḥ nainaṃ manuṣyāḥ paśyanti paśyanti tridivaukasaḥ
english: The little-learned conceal the sin they have knowingly committed; men do not see them, but the dwellers in heaven see them.

sanskrit: pāpena hi kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ pāpam evānuvartate dhārmikeṇa kṛto dharmaḥ kartāram anuvartate
english: For the sin done by the sinner follows after him as sin alone; and the dharma wrought by the righteous man follows after its doer.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ na smaratīha mūḍho; vivartamānasya tad eti kartuḥ rāhur yathā candram upaiti cāpi; tathābudhaṃ pāpam upaiti karma
english: The fool here remembers not the sin he has done; yet as the doer passes through his rebirths, it overtakes him—just as Rāhu comes upon the moon, so does the sinful deed come upon the witless man.

sanskrit: āśayā saṃcitaṃ dravyaṃ yat kāle neha bhujyate tad budhā na praśaṃsanti maraṇaṃ na pratīkṣate
english: Wealth heaped up in hope, that is not enjoyed here in its season—the wise do not commend it; for death does not wait.

sanskrit: mānasaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ tasmāt sarveṣu bhūteṣu manasā śivam ācaret
english: The wise declare that the dharma toward all beings is of the mind; therefore toward all beings one should bear oneself benevolently in mind.

sanskrit: eka eva cared dharmaṃ nāsti dharme sahāyatā kevalaṃ vidhim āsādya sahāyaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
english: Alone, each by himself, should one practise dharma; in dharma there is no fellowship. Once one has met one's appointed lot, what can a companion do?

sanskrit: devā yonir manuṣyāṇāṃ devānām amṛtaṃ divi pretyabhāve sukhaṃ dharmāc chaśvat tair upabhujyate
english: The gods are the source of men, and the nectar of the gods is in heaven; in the state after death, the happiness that springs from dharma is enjoyed by them everlastingly.
